page: Microsoft Azure M128ds_v2 is a high-memory virtual machine belonging to the MDSMediumMemoryv2 family, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by x86_64 Intel processors providing 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 2048 GB of system memory. With an allocation of 16 GB of RAM per core, this instance is configured to handle vast in-memory footprints directly on a single virtual host.

Storage capability on the instance includes 4398 GB of integrated local solid-state disk (SSD) storage, paired with full support for Azure Premium Storage. The bundled local SSD space supplies high-throughput, low-latency temporary capacity for database paging, tempdb workloads, and volatile caching. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, dedicating the physical node entirely to memory-centric and compute processes.

In terms of resource architecture, the M128ds_v2 offers high density that allows organizations to vertically scale workloads that would otherwise require complex distributed clustering. This consolidation reduces latency overhead inherent to multi-node networking. The primary tradeoff lies in operational concentration, as running workloads on a single 2-terabyte memory instance necessitates deliberate backup and high-availability planning.

Microsoft Azure M128ds_v2 is configured for mission-critical enterprise environments, such as large-scale in-memory relational databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive distributed caching tiers, and extensive transactional data engines.
description: Microsoft Azure M128ds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for demanding memory-bound workloads and enterprise database deployments. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel processors under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the system delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 2048 GB of system memory, yielding a substantial 16 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 4398 GB of fast local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations, catering to applications that require rapid temporary disk access and high throughput. Without hardware GPU accelerators, the instance directs all compute resources toward CPU and memory operations. The extensive resource density eliminates the complexity of multi-node horizontal scaling for workloads that require monolithic memory space, though running single massive instances represents an architectural concentration risk. Microsoft Azure M128ds_v2 is suited for large-scale in-memory relational databases, enterprise resource planning applications, heavy caching layers, and high-capacity data processing platforms.
